partner_context.their_ambition: Ruter runs public transport for Oslo and Akershus — metro, tram, bus and the fjord ferries — on one ticket, and it has committed to emission-free operations. It has already contracted the electrification of the Oslofjord express boats and the busy Aker Brygge–Nesoddtangen crossing, Norway's largest car-free ferry route. Its ambition on the water is a fully zero-emission fjord network.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling-electric upgrade to a fjord ferry network Ruter already runs and is already electrifying. The Nesoddtangen commuter crossing, the inner-fjord recreation islands and the Bygdøy museum link — flown clear of the water: faster, near-silent, low-wake and zero-emission, on the same Ruter ticket, from the piers that already exist.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Oslo, Norway · Ruter (Oslo & Akershus public transport)
hero.title: Navier × Oslo Ferries — the inner fjord, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on the Nesoddtangen commuter crossing and the inner-Oslofjord island network: faster, quieter and all-electric public transport across the fjord Ruter is already committed to decarbonising.
hero.what_we_do_together: Ruter brings the fjord ferry network, the piers and the public-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we run the same fjord — faster and zero-emission — extending the electrification Ruter has already begun.

why_now: Ruter has contracted the electrification of the Oslofjord express boats and the Nesoddtangen crossing, inside a city that targets a 95% cut in emissions by 2030. The commitment is made and the piers are in place; a foiling-electric fleet is how the fjord links get there at speed, with almost no wake through a busy, recreation-heavy inner fjord.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the Ruter network at Aker Brygge, where the fjord ferries meet the tram and bus. A single Ruter ticket carries a commuter from the centre straight onto a foil to Nesoddtangen or the islands — conventional ferries keep the heaviest car-and-freight runs underneath.

journeys_unlocked.label: Aker Brygge ↔ Nesoddtangen
journeys_unlocked.today: Norway's largest car-free ferry route — heavily used, and now being electrified with battery vessels.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The flagship commuter crossing, flown clear of the water — fast, near-silent, zero-emission, year-round.

journeys_unlocked.label: Aker Brygge ↔ Hovedøya
journeys_unlocked.today: A short seasonal hop to the inner-fjord recreation islands.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A low-wake, low-noise link that protects the inner fjord's swimming and recreation waters — clean and quiet by design.

journeys_unlocked.label: Aker Brygge ↔ Bygdøy
journeys_unlocked.today: A seasonal boat to the Bygdøy museum peninsula, otherwise a long road loop.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A direct zero-emission link to the Bygdøy museums, viable across a longer season on foils.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is purpose-built for this network: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (vital on shared and protected waters), near-silent, zero-emission, and viable year-round. It delivers the authority's published decarbonisation commitment on the links where speed and wake have kept older vessels in service.

proof_points.claim: Ruter has already contracted ferry electrification.
proof_points.evidence: Ruter's 2022 agreement with Norled electrifies the Oslofjord express boats; the Aker Brygge–Nesoddtangen route is Norway's largest car-free ferry route.

proof_points.claim: The fjord ferries are public transport, not tourism.
proof_points.evidence: Ruter runs the inner-fjord island ferries on the ordinary public-transport ticket, year-round to Nesoddtangen.
Oslo targets a 95% cut in greenhouse-gas emissions by 2030 — among the most ambitious municipal climate goals in Europe.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Can it run through an Oslofjord winter?
objections.response: The Nesoddtangen crossing runs year-round today and is already being electrified; foiling-electric routing is planned around ice and weather, and the platform's efficiency suits the shoulder season especially well.

objections.concern: Does it disturb the recreation islands?
objections.response: The opposite — low wake and near-silent running reduce disturbance to the inner-fjord swimming and recreation waters compared with today's diesel vessels.

objections.concern: Does this replace the ferries people rely on?
objections.response: No — it's a faster, cleaner layer on the same Ruter ticket; conventional and battery ferries keep the heaviest car-and-freight runs.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: The ferry route map, the piers/stops, the single-ticket integration, and the published decarbonisation mandate.
the_ask.next_step: Identify the first Ruter fjord link — most likely Aker Brygge–Nesoddtangen or a recreation-island line — for a foiling-electric public pilot on the Ruter ticket.

close.body: Ruter has already begun electrifying Oslo's fjord ferries. Navier is how the passenger links go further, faster — a quiet, zero-emission crossing to Nesoddtangen and the inner-fjord islands, on the same public ticket, and gentle on one of the city's most treasured recreation waters.
